question: Triangle \(ABC\) with \(AB=50\) and \(AC=10\) has area \(120.\) Let \(D\) be the midpoint of \(\overline{AB},\) and let \(E\) be the midpoint of \(\overline{AC}.\) The angle bisector of \(\angle BAC\) intersects \(\overline{DE}\) and \(\overline{BC}\) at \(F\) and \(G,\) respectively. What is the area of quadrilateral \(FDBG?\)
solution:
The angle bisector divides both \(DE\) and \(BC\) in the same ratio. This lets us compare \(FDBG\) with the whole trapezoid \(EDBC\).

Since \(D\) and \(E\) are midpoints, \(DE\parallel BC\), and \(\triangle ADE\) is similar to \(\triangle ABC\) with side-length ratio \(\tfrac12\). Its area is therefore
\[
\operatorname{Area}(ADE)=\left(\frac12\right)^2\cdot120=30.
\]
Removing this small triangle leaves
\[
\operatorname{Area}(EDBC)=120-30=90.
\]
The midpoint lengths are \(AD=25\) and \(AE=5\). Applying the Angle Bisector Theorem in \(\triangle ADE\) and \(\triangle ABC\) gives
\[
\frac{DF}{FE}=\frac{25}{5}=5,
\qquad
\frac{BG}{GC}=\frac{50}{10}=5.
\]
Thus
\[
DF=\frac56DE,
\qquad
BG=\frac56BC.
\]
The trapezoids \(FDBG\) and \(EDBC\) have the same height \(h\), the distance between the parallel lines \(DE\) and \(BC\). Using the trapezoid area formula,
\[
\frac{\operatorname{Area}(FDBG)}{\operatorname{Area}(EDBC)}
=\frac{\tfrac12(DF+BG)h}{\tfrac12(DE+BC)h}
=\frac56.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\operatorname{Area}(FDBG)=\frac56\cdot90=\boxed{75},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
